item.description:
Labwrk 1.1.20 installs updates on its own when **Automatically update** is on.
- **Updates install automatically:** Labwrk used to download updates in the background but wait to install them until you quit it, which rarely happens with a menu bar app. Now it installs a downloaded update right away and reopens itself on the new version. - **One last manual step:** this version is the last one that still waits for a quit. If it has already downloaded, choose **Quit Labwrk** and open Labwrk again to finish installing it. Later updates install without any action from you. - Leaves GitLab monitoring, project scope, notifications, and saved settings unchanged.
Requires macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon. This release is signed with Labwrk's own certificate and has not been Apple Developer ID signed or notarized, so macOS asks you to approve the first launch of a newly downloaded copy (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway). Update archives are independently Ed25519-signed and verified by Sparkle.

Labwrk 1.1.19 keeps the pipeline panel fully on screen when its menu bar icon sits near the right edge.
- **Panel always fully visible:** when the menu bar icon is far to the right, the panel used to open partly off the screen and get cut off. It now shifts left, or right, so the whole panel stays visible. - Leaves GitLab monitoring, project scope, notifications, and saved settings unchanged.
Requires macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon. This release is signed with Labwrk's own certificate and has not been Apple Developer ID signed or notarized, so macOS asks you to approve the first launch of a newly downloaded copy (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway). Update archives are independently Ed25519-signed and verified by Sparkle.

Labwrk 1.1.18 rides out GitLab requests that never get an answer, so stage warnings and refresh errors appear far less often.
- **Fewer “Stages unavailable” warnings:** GitLab.com occasionally leaves a single request unanswered. Labwrk now repeats a request that timed out once, right away, instead of showing the pipeline without stages until the next refresh. Reruns are never sent twice. - **Lighter on GitLab:** finished pipelines that haven’t changed keep the stages Labwrk already loaded, and everything reloads every five minutes. Each refresh now sends about half as many requests. - **Safer sign-in renewal:** renewing your GitLab sign-in now waits up to 90 seconds for a slow reply, because GitLab ends the old sign-in as soon as it handles a renewal. - **Refresh and View Log in warnings:** panel warnings now include **Refresh** to try again right away and **View Log** to show the diagnostic log in Finder. Refresh is hidden while you need to sign in or while GitLab’s rate limit is in effect. - **Refresh works after an error:** a manual refresh no longer waits out the automatic retry delay after a failed refresh. - Leaves GitLab monitoring, project scope, notifications, and saved settings unchanged.
